title: Observability contracts & ops weekly runbook (project slate)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working project slate to define 'observability contracts' between platform, serving-runtime, and SRE teams and to establish a lightweight weekly ops runbook for SLO enforcement experiments. The doc is intentionally pragmatic — aim for a 6‑week pilot that proves the contract model, validates staffing patterns, and produces an enforceable, low-friction runbook that feature teams can adopt.

Why this now:
- Increasing variance in tail latency and token-cost spikes across hosted inference routes; we need faster, clearer escalation paths.
- Multiple teams request consistent telemetry that they can rely on for SLOs without bespoke dashboards.
- We want to reduce on-call thrash by standardizing signals + automated triage steps.

Objectives (success criteria):
1) Define a minimal observability contract (metrics, traces, logs, alert semantics) that 3 pilot services adopt by the end of week 3.
2) Run a 6‑week ops experiment with a weekly runbook cadence and measure mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to mitigation (MTTM) improvement vs baseline.
3) Produce an ’ops kit’ (playbook + dashboards + alert templates + sample queries) that can be handed to feature teams.
4) Validate staffing pattern (1 primary SRE + 1 platform liaison per weekly window) and quantify burn rate.

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
In-scope:
- Platform-level exporter/metric naming conventions for model-serving endpoints (latency p50/p95/p99, request volume, error-rate, kv-cache hit ratio).
- Trace span conventions for request fanout (router -> runtime -> GPU-pool).
- A canonical set of alerts with severity mapping and runbook steps (P0/P1/P2).
- Weekly ops runbook template and rotation schedule for pilot services.
Out-of-scope:
- Full SLO negotiations for every product route (we will onboard 3 pilot routes only).
- Extensive backend refactor work — preference for adapter-layer fixes or dashboards until contract proves value.

Pilot participants (teams & services):
- Serving-runtime: model-inference-service (pilots: text-gen-prod, embeddings-prod)
- Platform-engineering: metrics-exporter, alert-router
- SRE (stability): primary on-call cohort + reliability liaison
- Product-hosted-api: route owners for two high-volume routes

Deliverables and timeline (6 weeks):
Week 0 (kickoff): finalize contract spec doc and share with stakeholders; align on pilot routes.
Week 1: implement metric exporters and tracing tags for pilot routes; prototype dashboards.
Week 2: deploy alert templates to staging; run tabletop
Week 3: cutover alerts to pilot incidents (low-impact window); collect MTTA/MTTM baseline
Week 4: iterate on runbook steps and automations (prefill remediation links, one-click rollback patch)
Week 5: stress/chaos probe to validate escalation chain; measure signal fidelity
Week 6: retro + ops kit handoff + decision: iterate vs scale

Weekly runbook template (to be used during pilot):
- Monday: health snapshot + triage (owner: platform liaison)
- Tuesday: capacity forecast + top-3 anomaly review (owner: serving-runtime lead)
- Wednesday: policy & routing check (owner: product-hosted-api)
- Thursday: automation chore (deploy small alert tuning/KB update)
- Friday: incident retro + metrics capture for week (owner: SRE)
- Weekend on-call: standby with explicit escalation ladder (primary SRE -> platform engineer on-call -> product owner)

Observability contract - minimal spec (one-page summary):
Metrics (all exported with tags: service, route, model_version, region):
- request.count (per-second counter)
- request.latency.{p50,p95,p99} (histogram/summary)
- request.error_rate (ratio + 5xx/4xx breakdown)
- kv_cache.hit_ratio (gauge)
- gpu.utilization (gauge)
Trace semantics:
- Root span: request_id, route, model_version
- Child spans: router_lookup, runtime_inference, gpu_scheduler
- Include sampled logs on error spans (stacktrace + model input hash)
Logs:
- Structured JSON with keys: ts, request_id, route, user_tier, error_code, latency_ms
Alerting semantics (starter):
- P0: sustained p99 > 2x target for 3 minutes or error_rate > 5% for 1 minute -> immediate page to SRE
- P1: sustained p95 > 1.5x target for 10 minutes -> page to platform liaison
- P2: metric deviation but below P1 thresholds -> email/async review

Runbook example (P0):
1) Acknowledge and post incident in #platform-observability with incident template.
2) Triage: check recent deploys, config changes, hot-path metrics (kv_cache, gpu.util), and trace head.
3) If rollbackable deploy detected in last 10 minutes -> rollback to previous stable version and observe for 5 minutes.
4) If capacity-bound -> trigger autoscale or re-route to dedicated pool and notify product owner.

Staffing experiment (measurement plan):
- Rotation model: 1 week windows, primary SRE + platform liaison. Run three cohorts across 6 weeks (each cohort 2 weeks).
- Metrics collected: MTTA, MTTM, number of false positives, number of escalations to product.
- Burn measurement: hours logged per incident and week (tracked in a shared sheet).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Too many noisy alerts -> mitigation: hold baseline tuning week and add smart dampening rules.
- Risk: Teams view contract as prescriptive -> mitigation: make contract additive and allow opt-outs for experimental routes with a short LOE checklist.
- Risk: Missing telemetry from GPU pools -> mitigation: fallback to edge metrics + synthetic checks while engineering fix is tracked.

Instrumentation checklist (developer-facing):
- Add standardized metric names and tags (link: confluence:PLATFORM-OBS-CONTRACTS-2027)
- Add trace span naming and ensure request_id header flows through all services
- Wire alerts to alert-router slack channel with attachments and runbook link

Success measurement (after pilot):
- 20% reduction in MTTA and 15% reduction in MTTM vs baseline, or clearly documented blockers preventing improvement.
- At least 2 feature teams adopt the ops kit within 30 days of handoff.
- A lightweight contract PR template and onboarding checklist created and reviewed.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Which 3 pilot routes are the highest-impact but lowest-risk for cutover? (ask product owners to nominate)
- SLA targets: should we use strict p99 goals for all routes or tier them by user_tier?
- Which tooling for synthetic checks — existing uptime probes or new headless inference runner?

Next actions (owner tags):
- Aisha: finalize contract one-pager and schedule kickoff (by 2027-02-22).
- Marco: prepare exporter changes for route tags and a small dashboard (by 2027-02-25).
- Priya: draft alert templates and Slack incident template (by 2027-02-24).
- Jenna: set up trial rotation calendar and log sheet (by 2027-02-26).

Notes to self (working):
- Keep this doc short; the canonical contract should be 1 page + checklist.
- Expect pushback on tagging overhead; have adapter pattern notes ready.
- We may want to include a brief legal/compliance check for routes that handle regulated data.

Appendix (links & quick refs):
- Pilot sign-up form (internal) -> https://forms.internal/redwood/obs-pilot
- Contract draft (confluence) -> confluence:PLATFORM-OBS-CONTRACTS-2027
- Baseline metrics sheet -> https://sheets.internal/redwood/obs-baseline-q1-2027

If you're reading this and want to join the pilot, drop a note in #platform-observability or ping me directly.

-- Aisha
